title: Flux 3 X Mimic Bridges Video Generation and Robotics
summary: Black Forest Labs&\#x27; Flux 3 multimodal model, combined with the Mimic video-action model, extracts world representations from video generation to enable robotic control. The system has been deployed at Audi and shows promising results in real-world manipulation tasks. This work demonstrates that video generation and physical AI share a unified foundation, potentially reducing the data requirements for robotic learning and accelerating the deployment of intelligent agents in the real world. It also marks a significant step toward general-purpose robots that can understand and interact with their environment. Flux 3 is a multimodal frontier model that jointly learns from images, video, and audio, while Mimic is a Video-Action Model \(VAM\) that grounds robotic policies in pretrained video models. However, the extracted representations are less disentangled than specialized approaches, which may limit performance on tasks requiring precise world understanding.
context: World models are AI systems that build internal representations of the physical world, including space, time, physics, and causality. Traditional Vision-Language-Action Models \(VLAs\) for robotics rely on static web data and must infer dynamics solely from robot trajectories. This new approach leverages the implicit world understanding in video generation models to provide richer priors for robotic control, bridging content creation and physical AI.
discussion: Community comments are generally positive, with users impressed by the robot&\#x27;s ability to resolve tricky tasks like reseating window trim after multiple attempts. One commenter notes the approach is not entirely new but praises its execution, while another criticizes the phrasing &\#x27;less disentangled representations&\#x27; as confusing. There is also appreciation for the partnership between European startups.
